'''Virtual Legacy''' is the [[Players Committee]] Virtual card pool from the [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]] to the [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]]. It is packaged as '''Virtual Blocks''' ([[Virtual Block 1]] through [[Virtual Block 9]]) and Legacy [[Virtual Shields]]. The cards are no longer valid for current Standard / [[Open]] constructed play; they remain the pool for [[Legacy Open]].

The predecessor era is [[Virtual Original]]. Pre-reorg numbered slips are on [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]. Current Virtual numbering after the Reset starts at [[Virtual Set 0]]. Era map: [[History of the Players Committee]].

== From numbered Virtual Sets ==

From 2002 through early 2009 the Players Committee published printable Virtual game-text slips as numbered Virtual Sets (VS1&ndash;VS17).<ref name="vslips">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual slips], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20131211224951/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/resources/virtual-slips/ Internet Archive] (11 December 2013)</ref><ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260930145354/https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Internet Archive]</ref> The first set was announced 12 February 2002 and tournament-legal Saturday, 9 March 2002.<ref name="tfn2002" /><ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Wayback)</ref>

Players sleeved the PDF cutouts over Decipher cards. Fifth Anthology was previewed as the 18th Virtual Set in June 2009. It never shipped as a standalone VirtualCards18.pdf. Its preview titles shipped inside Reflections IV / [[Virtual Block 6]]. Full VS18 story: [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]].

== 2009 Block reorganization ==

In August and September 2009 the Players Committee regrouped the numbered Virtual Sets into six thematic Virtual Blocks.<ref name="reorg2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090918131415/http://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org homepage], Wayback 18 September 2009</ref> VirtualBlock1.pdf, stamped Official text as of 7 December 2009, describes the change (Blocks 2&ndash;5 carry the same text):<ref name="blockreorg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf VirtualBlock1.pdf] (official text as of 7 December 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250925215932/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf Internet Archive]</ref>

: ''“Since the reorganization of the previous 18 virtual sets, there are now six blocks structured by theme. The first three blocks cover the classic trilogy, block 4 expands the expanded universe, the fifth block buffs the Old Republic, and block 6 is a mix - Reflections IV.”''

The Blocks repackaged the pre-Reset pool. Titles, frames, errata, and which cards remain legal can differ from the numbered Virtual Set PDFs.

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170705013057/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterLS.pdf Internet Archive] (5 July 2017)</ref>

September 2009 on Blocks 1&ndash;6 is the reorganization date; those cards were first released across 2002&ndash;2009 as Virtual Sets 1&ndash;18.

[[Virtual Shields]] is the Legacy / Block packaging of Defensive Shields (Original-era slips: [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]]), grouped as Virtual Block Defensive Shields in September/October 2009.

== Later blocks (7&ndash;9) ==

Blocks 7&ndash;9 are post-reorg expansions.

* '''[[Virtual Block 7]]''' (Darkness Rising / Ultimate series). First subset Virtual Set 7.1 Ultimate Power came out on 18 June 2010.<ref name="vb71pdf" /><ref name="vb71forum" /> The Polish fan site star-wars.pl reported it on 27 June 2010.<ref name="vb71">[https://star-wars.pl/News/12035,Premiera_Virtual_Block_7_1_Ultimate_Power.html Premiera Virtual Block 7.1 Ultimate Power], star-wars.pl. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20150524083017/http://www.star-wars.pl/News/12035,Premiera_Virtual_Block_7_1_Ultimate_Power.html Internet Archive] (24 May 2015)</ref> Later subsets: 7.2 Ultimate Freedom (released 13 December 2010; tournament legal 29 December 2010); 7.3 Ultimate Conflict (3 June 2011); 7.4 Ultimate Legacy (16 December 2011).
* '''[[Virtual Block 8]]''' (Scoundrels). First subset Virtual Set 8.1 Scoundrels, May 2012.<ref name="vb81">[https://web.archive.org/web/20120510015711/http://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org homepage], Wayback 10 May 2012</ref> Later subsets: 8.2 Agents For Hire (20 September 2012); 8.3 A Wretched Hive (March 2013 window).
* '''[[Virtual Block 9]]''' (Republic At War). Virtual Set 9.1 ''Republic at War'' was released 10 January 2014 and legal immediately.<ref name="vb91">[https://web.archive.org/web/20140115143606/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/v-set-9-1-is-live/ V-Set 9.1 is Live], starwarsccg.org (Wayback 15 January 2014)</ref> Virtual Set 9.2 was not released in its then-current form; the Reset announcement cancelled that plan in favor of a mini Worlds set that was remolded later. Details: [[Cancelled Virtual Sets]].

== Organized play ==

Championship constructed used the Block pool through the [[2014 World Championship]] in Toronto.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210624200645/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> That event is the last championship circuit on the pre-Reset pool. The constructed label is [[Legacy Open]].

== Online play ==

[[Holotable]] remained the usual downloaded tabletop through this era. Players enforced the rules; Holodeck built the decks.<ref name="c1ght">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/holotable-playing-star-wars-ccg-online-the-setup/ Holotable - Playing Star Wars CCG Online - The Setup], Category One Games. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20220926090936/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/holotable-playing-star-wars-ccg-online-the-setup/ Internet Archive]</ref> The Players Committee listed Holotable on its software page by 13 December 2013.<ref name="pcsoft">[https://web.archive.org/web/20131213094334/http://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/software/ Software], starwarsccg.org (Wayback, 13 December 2013)</ref> Version 0.9.9, announced 2 December 2014, handled the virtual card reset.<ref name="ht2014">[https://web.archive.org/web/20141217162132/http://www.holotable.com/ holotable.com homepage], Wayback 17 December 2014. News dated 12/2/14.</ref> [[GEMP]] came later.

== Rules and card types ==

During this era the Players Committee published [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]]. That book introduced the [[Mission]] card type.<ref name="ar20">[[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]]</ref> Missions appear on some Virtual Block 7, 8, and 9 cards. Advanced Rulebook 2.0 is distinct from the current [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]].

== Design ==

Block packaging grouped cards by theme: classic trilogy, Expanded Universe, Old Republic, and a Reflections IV mix.<ref name="blockreorg" /> Later expansions used subset releases (6.3 Mercenaries; 7.1&ndash;7.4; 8.1&ndash;8.3; 9.1). [[Virtual Block 5]] and [[Virtual Block 9]] emphasize Old Republic and Clone Wars material. Block slips carry a numbered diamond expansion icon. Some Block PDFs print one overlay for both an original title and its [[Alternate Image]] printing.

[[Jeremy Gardner]] of the Graphic Design Team authored the February 2014 Master List PDFs.<ref name="masterds" /><ref name="masterls" />

== Printable Master Lists ==

The combined printable master of the pre-Reset virtual pool is two Players Committee PDFs titled '''''Virtual Cards: Master List''''' (Dark Side 59 pages; Light Side 54 pages):

* [[:File:Virtual Legacy Final Master DS.pdf]]
* [[:File:Virtual Legacy Final Master LS.pdf]]

Internet Archive captured the Players Committee Resources copies of the Dark Side and Light Side Master Lists in July 2017:

* [https://web.archive.org/web/20170704232650/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf MasterDS.pdf] (Wayback 4 July 2017 of [http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf])
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20170705013057/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterLS.pdf MasterLS.pdf] (Wayback 5 July 2017 of [http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterLS.pdf starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterLS.pdf])

The cover banner is '''Official text as of 27 April 2013'''. The files are dated '''3 February 2014''' (author Jeremy Gardner, Graphic Design Team; copyright SWCCG Players Committee 2014), after Virtual Set 9.1 and before the Reset announcement.<ref name="masterds" /><ref name="masterls" /> They hold the up-to-date text of every Players Committee virtual card, sorted alphabetically by card type. The slips are printable, to sleeve over original cards. Some slips supersede earlier Virtual Block presentations of the same titles.

An HTML type list of the same combined pool is [https://res.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VMasterType.html VMasterType.html].<ref name="vmaster">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VMasterType.html Virtual Master type list], res.starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20201030095838/https://res.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VMasterType.html Internet Archive] (30 October 2020)</ref> The current Players Committee Legacy format page is starwarsccg.org/legacy/ (updated 30 July 2022).<ref name="pclegacy">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/legacy/ Legacy], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020195330/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/legacy.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The July 2014 Reset announcement said Legacy would keep all pre-Reset Virtual cards in a Master Legacy PDF (a fixed pool unless later Design &amp; Development work supported Legacy balance).<ref name="reset-announce">[http://web.archive.org/web/20141020142523id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/reset-of-standard-format/ Reset of Standard Format] (Wayback id_ capture), byline 25 July 2014</ref>

== 2014 Reset ==

On 25 July 2014 the Advocate Council published '''''Reset of Standard Format''''' and chose a complete reset of the virtual card pool rather than a cleanup / mass errata.<ref name="reset-announce" /> ''The Ringer'' later reported that the virtual pool had grown to about 1,100 cards.<ref name="ringer">[https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This 'Star Wars' Subculture], Ben Lindbergh, ''The Ringer'', 21 May 2018. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20180523173054/https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community Internet Archive]</ref> [[Chris Gogolen]] and others spent five months deciding which cards to keep.<ref name="ringer" /> [[Scott Lingrell]] later called the Reset the best thing the committee could have done.<ref name="ringer" /> New Standard used a small base set (later [[Virtual Set 0]]) and new Virtual set numbering. Pre-Reset Virtual cards became the [[Legacy Open|Legacy]] format. Follow-up legal lists (Virtual Set 0 and Virtual Set 1 Preview) were posted 25 September 2014. Main article: [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]].

The [[2014 World Championship]] (21&ndash;24 August 2014, Toronto) was the last championship circuit on the old Block pool.<ref name="afg" />
